correctness.rationale: Exact graph, edge-subset predicate and finite face set reconstructed. Two independent face enumerations agree on all 3,149 augmented faces and 1,096 forbidden matching triples. Deterministic element matching gives 1,552 disjoint augmented pairs, 45 critical dimension-three cells, and complete directed Hasse acyclicity on 11,832 covers. Removing the empty-face pair gives one critical zero-cell and 45 dimension-three cells; the separate 11,808-cover nonaugmented acyclicity check passes. Standard integral discrete-Morse theory then gives a wedge of 45 three-spheres, with no unverified integral attaching boundary.

value.rationale: The graph is the distinguished Levi graph of the (8_3) Möbius–Kantor configuration and is a canonical cubic bipartite graph. Matching threshold three is the first higher non-matching stage beyond pairwise incidence. Recent bipartite edge-addition theory guarantees persistent degree-three classes for a graph with six-cycles, but neither rank 45 nor a homotopy wedge. The exact integral classification gives a motivated finite sharp-degree benchmark and an independently reproducible finite collapse/matching certificate. No general family theorem is needed for this self-contained natural invariant to be useful.
